Subject: Azure private plan - initial term sheet

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is Snowbridge's draft term sheet for an Azure private plan and co-sell engagement. High level: we want a private marketplace listing, co-sell lead sharing, and a committed minimum monthly usage (12 months) with volume tiers.

Key asks we flagged in the doc:
- 45/55 revenue split on co-sell influenced deals (Snowbridge/Redwood) with clear definition of 'co-sell influenced'
- Data residency: US only for production data used in the integration
- Audit rights clause limited to annual, scoped to billing records only
- Termination for convenience: 90 days, pro-rata refunds for committed usage

Can you route this to legal and procurement for an initial read? We're hoping to get a commercial agreement and listing live by mid-August.

Attachments: SB_Azure_Private_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term sheet, 6 pages)

Thanks,
Taylor Nguyen

Hi Taylor —

Appreciate the term sheet and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (GTM/partner ops) and Jonas (legal) to kick off internal review. High-level reactions from my side:

- Revenue split: we usually target a co-sell influenced split closer to 60/40 in favor of the Marketplace partner when the partner brings the ARR; need examples of what Snowbridge considers 'influence' (lead owner, lead stage, sourced vs influenced).
- Commitment: 12-month commits are OK, but our standard private plan commitment language ties discounts to usage bands and has a 30–60 day cure period for missed commits.
- Data residency: US-only is fine for hosted customers, but we need to confirm any telemetry/metrics that may route to EU for infra telemetry — Jonas please confirm.
- Audit rights: we prefer access to billing and telemetry for audit limited to two reviewers and encrypted transit.

Proposed next step: Jonas, can you do a redline of the term sheet and capture any standard RD/indemnity/IP exceptions? Laura, can you estimate listing timeframes and check marketplace co-sell checklist (I attached our internal checklist). Taylor — can we set a 30-min call Thurs morning to align on revenue definition and commits?

Thanks,
Alex

On Tue, Jul 7, 2026 at 11:02 AM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Appreciate the term sheet and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (GTM/partner ops) and Jonas (legal) to kick off internal review.

Taylor / Snowbridge team — attaching our annotated redlines. High level legal positions (summarized):

1) Revenue split: Acceptable to negotiate to a 55/45 split in favor of Snowbridge for deals where Snowbridge is the primary seller and owns the lead through to contract signature. For 'influenced' deals (Redwood sources lead or does >30% of opportunity management) we propose 65/35 in Redwood's favor. Need definitions in SOW/sales playbook.

2) Commitment and refunds: We will accept a 12-month usage commitment but insist on a quarterly reconciliation and a 60-day cure for shortfalls before applying true-ups. Pro-rata refunds only for prepaid credits; otherwise, future credits apply.

3) Data residency and telemetry: We can agree to US-only storage for customer data; operational telemetry (metrics about runtime performance) will be aggregated and scrubbed of account identifiers before any cross-region transfer.

4) Audit scope: limit to billing and invoicing records and only once per 12 months. Any additional audit requests need a subpoena or equivalent.

5) Indemnity/IP: standard mutual IP indemnity with carve-outs for open-source and third-party frameworks. Also propose a 1-year liability cap tied to average quarterly spend.

I've attached SB_Azure_Redlines_JW.docx with inline comments and proposed contractual language. Happy to walk through on the call.

Attachments: SB_Azure_Redlines_JW.docx (redlines and suggested contract language)

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — that level of detail is helpful and mostly inline with our expectations. A couple quick clarifications inline:

- Revenue split: Snowbridge can accept the 55/45 as a baseline for partner-sourced deals; we'd like a short appendix that lists the attribution rules (lead owner, MQL->SQL handoff timing, and CRM tagging).
- Commit refunds: We prefer a single pro-rata refund for prepayment if termination for convenience occurs within the first 6 months — otherwise credits. Can Redwood confirm whether that can be accommodated?
- Audit wording: the limitation to billing records is fine; Snowbridge's procurement team will ask for one operational spot-check during onboarding — can we make that explicit?

We're OK to move to docu-sign after the final redline pass. Here's the DocuSign preliminary envelope we can use: https://www.docusign.com/submit/SB-AZ-2026 (will be populated once legal confirms final language).

Proposed next steps:
- Jonas to send final redline by EOD Mon (12 Jul)
- Alex / Laura to confirm marketplace listing timeline and co-sell enablement checklist by Wed (14 Jul)
- Target live private listing: week of Aug 17

Thanks — Taylor
